Hi Vanessa,

We're onboarding Redwood for a short-term HIPAA audit tied to a customer investigation (internal ticket: ClinicalAudit-47). Compliance is asking us to preserve logs and backups related to this project for an extra period beyond our current contract window. Specifically: can Redwood pause automated backup pruning and hold immutable snapshots for up to 120 days for the ClinicalAudit-47 dataset?

We expect the hold to affect KV logs, request/response traces for the project, and daily backups in the us-west region. Two quick asks:
- Can you confirm whether such a hold will require a DPA amendment / DocuSign annex and what the procurement path looks like?
- We also need a current list of subprocessors involved in storing backups and logs (including any cross-border transfer subprocessors).

Can someone on your side outline operational steps and cost impact? We may route the DPA amendment through procurement once we have scope.

Thanks,

Samir — thanks for the heads up. We can support a temporary hold for the ClinicalAudit-47 assets; below is a short options summary and the next steps we typically follow: 

Operational options (tradeoffs):
1) Account-level erase circuit-breaker: pause all automated deletion/purge jobs for the account and surface a manual review queue. Minimal infra change, full pause. Recommended if you need immediate stop.
2) Immutable snapshot buffer: create read-only snapshots of the affected buckets and retain them for N days (does not block hot-path KV pruning unless you request separate log-hold). Good for backup-level preservation.
3) Hybrid two-phase: snapshot + stage gate for phased prune with manual signoff (we've used this for regulated audits).

Legal/contract: a DPA annex (DocuSign amendment) is preferred for holds longer than 30 days that deviate from contracted retention. Kimberly will confirm language and subprocessors.

Can you confirm whether the hold must include live request logs (full traces) or only backups + daily aggregates? Also confirm exact start date you want (we can backdate to today if necessary).

If you want, Marissa can draft the operational runbook and estimated cost delta. Once agreed, Kimberly will issue the DPA Annex and procurement can countersign.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Samir — looping in Legal. A few clarifying points before we draft an annex:

1) Scope: please itemize the datasets (bucket names, project ids) that need the hold. A scoped hold is preferable to an account-wide pause.
2) Duration: Vanessa mentioned 30+ days triggers an annex — please confirm target days. Our default annex templates cover up to 180 days with an option to extend subject to review.
3) Subprocessors: we have the following that touch backups/logs: S3-compatible object store (managed by CloudStore Inc.), long-term escrow snapshots (SnapshotVault Ltd.), and cross-border transfer via SecureRelay Partners (EU-US routing). If you need a full subprocessor attestation, we'll attach annex B.
4) Data minimization/redaction: Will Acme require raw request traces with PII, or would redacted logs suffice for the audit? If raw PII is required, we will add a controls clause in the annex and may need additional safeguards (KMS/HSM key scoping).

I've attached a draft annex (DPA_Annex_B.pdf) with placeholders for dataset ids and duration. Please confirm scope and whether procurement needs an estimated cost line item.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: DPA_Annex_B.pdf (draft annex with subprocessor list)

A couple of constraints from our side:
- The hold should be isolated to the ClinicalAudit-47 project (we'll give exact project ids).
- Procurement will need a CAPEX/opex estimate before signing any annex.

Would Redwood consider the following workflow?
1) Immediately enable account-level circuit-breaker for ClinicalAudit-47 to stop purge jobs.
2) Create immutable snapshots of the last 90 days worth of backups and tag them with a hold flag.
3) Hold KV logs (live append-only) for 120 days, then trigger a staged prune with manual signoff.

Please advise on operational feasibility and expected cost range.

— Samir

Samir — ops proposal and quick cost sketch below. Sorry for the long email, wanted to be operationally precise.

Proposal (two-phase, isolated to ClinicalAudit-47):
Phase A (immediate, day 0):
- Execute account-scoped erase circuit-breaker for the project only (CLI: redwood ops hold apply --project ClinicalAudit-47 --mode circuit-breaker).
- Snapshot last 90 days of backups as immutable objects with hold tag. Snapshots stored in SnapshotVault (our escrow partner).
- Flag KV logs to disable automated TTL rotations for the flagged partitions.

Phase B (day 120):
- Manual prune window: after day 120 we will prepare a prune plan and hold a signoff call with Acme compliance + Redwood legal/ops (2 business-day SLA to produce plan).
- Gradual prune (if approved): prune in 7-day windows with forensic export retained for 30 days post-prune.

Estimated cost delta (ballpark):
- Snapshot escrow storage + immutability: ~$1,200–$1,800 per 1TB-month (depends on snapshot count).
- Ops handling and manual signoff: one-time $3,500 engagement fee (covers runbook, manual prune coordination, and audit logs export).
- Temporary KV TTL disable: negligible infra cost, operational risk assessment included.

Attachments: backup_schedule_estimate.csv (spreadsheet with per-TB estimates)

Operational notes:
- We will need a signed DPA Annex for the 120-day hold prior to creating immutable snapshots (legal requirement).
- If Acme requests raw request traces with PII, we'll need scoped KMS adjustments (additional cost).
- We can backdate the hold to 2026-10-18 if you confirm in writing before EOD.

If this workflow looks right, I can produce the exact CLI snippet and a runbook and Kimberly can circulate the annex for signature.

Marissa Cole
